entries.summary: The activation marker for Cowork mode; selected by this env var, not a CLI flag (--cowork itself is rejected at agent-invocation time, plugin-scope only). entries.name: CLAUDE_CODE_ALWAYS_ENABLE_EFFORT

entries.name: CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_APPEND_SUBAGENT_PROMPT
entries.summary: Gates appendSubagentSystemPrompt on the initialize control-request (subagent system-prompt append). Set unconditionally to "1" in every Cowork spawn env (Desktop-side) -- and this is REQUIRED, not just sufficient: consumption requires BOTH the env var AND initialize.appendSubagentSystemPrompt (pt(process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_APPEND_SUBAGENT_PROMPT)&&r.options.appendSubagentSystemPrompt). The CLI's own self-set helper (YRp) that flips this env var on has exactly one call site -- the hidden --append-subagent-system-prompt CLI flag path -- it is NOT invoked by the initialize handler itself. So an SDK/driver that sends the option over initialize without independently setting the env var in the agent's process env gets no append.

provenance.note: confirmed unconditional Cowork spawn-env injection + the initialize-delivery env-gate dependency (YRp only fires on the hidden flag path, not on initialize)

entries.name: CLAUDE_CODE_ENVIRONMENT_KIND
entries.summary: Deployment-type tag: byoc | anthropic_cloud | bridge; drives the classifier-summary surface map (byoc adds "ccr", bridge adds "bridge"). CONFIRMED mechanism (L119): the "bridge" value is set exclusively by the agent's OWN claude remote-control bridge worker (a poll/ack/stop client against /v1/environments/{id}/work) when it spawns a child CLI process to run a claimed work item -- the Desktop never assigns this value itself (0 spawn-env assignments found in either Desktop build). A Desktop-hosted bridge session reaches the same "bridge" classifier surface via a separate signal, the in-process flag replBridgeActive (qR()), not this env var -- the surface map ORs both. byoc/anthropic_cloud are sibling environment-PROVIDER kinds of the same /v1/environment_providers API and feed the "ccr" surface, not "bridge".

provenance.note: mechanism confirmed: set by the agent's own remote-control bridge worker at child-spawn time, not by the Desktop; Desktop-hosted bridge sessions reach the same surface via replBridgeActive instead

Mirrors can_use_tool for host-side routing."). Scope is gated by IQo(e){return e.decideLocation==="pre-ask"} -- fires ONLY for automatic rule/mode/classifier denials evaluated agent-locally before the host is ever asked. Does NOT fire for interactive can_use_tool asks the host answers deny, and does NOT fire for PreToolUse-hook denials (those surface as an is_error tool_result instead). Carries no tool_input/path field. Consequence for Cowork: the host-loop path-gate (PreToolUse hook + canUseTool wrapper) never produces this event -- a corroborating source for pre-ask denials only, never the sole source of path-denial observability.

entries.summary: Promoted from speculative to confirmed. Lesson 46 catalogued this only as an unreleased precedence-order entry with no evidence anything set it. Full mechanism (L124): Desktop injects it CONDITIONALLY -- only when server-side YukonSilverConfig.defaultSubagentModel (IPC setYukonSilverConfig) is not the "inherit" sentinel; when "inherit", the env var is omitted entirely (by default a Cowork Task sub-agent runs the same model as the main loop). Fork dispatches force-inherit: the Agent-tool never forwards its own model param on a fork call (model:B?void 0:m), so a fork always resolves via frontmatter/inherit regardless of this env var.

entries.name: Task
entries.summary: Subagent dispatch. Continuation lives elsewhere: SendMessage resume (tool.SendMessage), subagent_type 'fork' (inherits full conversation context), Workflow resumeFromRunId. Type-less dispatch (subagent_type omitted) falls back to the built-in general-purpose type with tools:["*"] -- the FULL wildcard tool surface, including mcp__workspace__bash in Cowork host-loop; production audit-log evidence shows this fallback firing routinely (113 of 509 real dispatches across 39 sessions on one machine carried no subagent_type at all). Depth cap 5 (NMr host / BLr in-VM), enforced by hiding the Agent/Task tool itself from a sub-agent's own composed toolset once agentDepth>=5; no Task-specific fan-out/concurrency cap exists anywhere in either binary -- the only bound on parallel sub-agent starts is the generic env.CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_TOOL_USE_CONCURRENCY scheduler window.

entries.name: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT
entries.summary: Template token + injected env var resolving to the plugin's own --plugin-dir (agent sets CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT: t.path). Under Cowork the Desktop picks the dir per mode: Ei = isHostLoopModeEnabled ? qX(installPath) : sdkPath. Host-loop (production) => host-side claude-hostloop-plugins/<hash> staging path, accepted by host file tools (Read/Edit/Glob/Grep) but useless to in-VM bash (mcp__workspace__bash), which must use the VM mount /sessions/<id>/mnt/.local-plugins|.remote-plugins/... instead. VM-loop (requireCoworkFullVmSandbox orgs, whole agent in-VM) => sdkPath = that VM mount, so bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/x.sh works. Decisive: claude-hostloop-plugins is absent from both agent binaries (host CLI 2.1.201, in-VM ELF 2.1.197), present only in app.asar, so L89's 'host-side EVERYWHERE' is host-loop-only. Host-loop qX mechanics: space-triggered (returns the raw install path unless it contains a space) and deterministic (sha256(installPath).slice(0,16), stable across invocations/sessions/reboots). Third minor site: injected into a plugin-owned MCP server's headersHelper exec env. Host-loop mechanics live-confirmed 2026-07-07 (exact sha256(installPath)[:16] match + cross-session stability via docs/internal/cowork-pluginroot-probe); VM-loop resolution static-derived from the branch.

entries.name: mcp__plugins__list_plugins
entries.summary: Desktop SDK-MCP: render installed plugins as a widget. inputSchema {keywords[], context_label} required:[]; context_label is display-only and does not filter. Server isEnabled: sessionType==='cowork' && pluginsEnabled!==false. In allowedTools.

entries.name: mcp__plugins__search_plugins
entries.summary: Desktop SDK-MCP: search installable plugins. REQUIRED userIntent (natural language, verbatim/lightly paraphrased, NOT pre-tokenized) + optional keywords[], includeInstalled, trigger (shared Lr enum user_asked|proactive — UNGATED here, unlike suggest_skills). In allowedTools.

entries.name: mcp__plugins__suggest_plugin_install
entries.summary: Desktop SDK-MCP: render an inline plugin install card. REQUIRED contextLabel (3-5 words) + plugins[] (each REQUIRED pluginName/pluginId/description, optional backendId/skills[]). In allowedTools.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-registry__search_mcp_registry
entries.summary: Desktop SDK-MCP: search the MCP connector registry (searchDirectoryServers, .slice(0,10)). Server isEnabled: getDeploymentMode().type!=='3p' — the only discovery server NOT scoped to the cowork lane. In allowedTools.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-registry__suggest_connectors
entries.summary: Desktop SDK-MCP: suggest connectors to install/reconnect. REQUIRED uuids[] (directoryUuid, or the UUID portion of mcp__{uuid}__{tool} when reconnecting a failed tool) + optional keywords[] (single brand-stripped lowercase noun; renders as 'For your {keyword}'). In allowedTools.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-registry__list_connectors
entries.summary: Desktop SDK-MCP: list installed connectors; inputSchema {keywords[]} required:[]. In allowedTools.

entries.name: mcp__cowork-onboarding__show_onboarding_role_picker
entries.summary: Desktop SDK-MCP: render a role-picker chip row during Cowork onboarding; call with NO args (role/dismissed are 'populated by the permission flow'). Fifth discovery server (serverName qr='cowork-onboarding'), isEnabled sessionType==='cowork' && isFeatureEnabled('2114777685') (force-ON live). Rendered in 1264 real init.tools records since agent 2.1.92. NOT in allowedTools — routed through the permission prompt.

Gates the fifth SDK-MCP discovery server 'cowork-onboarding' (tool show_onboarding_role_picker) alongside sessionType==='cowork'. Live on/force (ruleId fr_mnj0h9xm, fcache 2026-07-24). Distinct from L131's four new-but-fcache-absent gate ids.
